true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Invalid ERB Ruby prevents rendering existing discussions

The tag `<%- end if %>` is invalid Ruby: the block should close with `end`, without the trailing `if`. Every embed request that finds an existing topic will fail with a template syntax error instead of displaying the discussion. The controller tests stub rendering, so they do not catch this; add a test that renders this view.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Feed polling assumes every entry has Atom-style content

Valid RSS entries can provide their body through `description` or `content:encoded`, and Atom entries can contain only a summary. For these entries, `i.content` is absent, so accessing it or calling `scrub` fails and aborts the entire polling run. The same exception also prevents `TopicRetriever` from reaching its HTTP fallback when feed polling is enabled. Select the supported body fields with a fallback and handle entries without a body; test actual RSS and Atom fixtures rather than only delegation to `poll_feed`.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

false_positives.candidate:
Automatic redirects bypass the embed host restriction

`TopicRetriever` checks only the hostname of the initial URL, but `open(url)` follows redirects to other hosts without repeating that check. An allowlisted URL that redirects to an internal HTTP endpoint therefore causes the worker to fetch that endpoint and potentially publish its contents as a topic. Validate redirect destinations and resolved addresses before connecting, or disable automatic redirects and handle them through a restricted fetcher.

Raw HTML posts bypass sanitization on import and subsequent edits

Returning `raw` directly makes external HTML executable forum content. `PollFeed` passes feed HTML to `TopicEmbed.import`, which only parses and rewrites URLs with Nokogiri; it does not remove scripts, event handlers, or unsafe URL schemes. These posts are then rendered as trusted cooked HTML. Subsequent edits also retain the raw-HTML cook method, allowing an author who can edit an imported post to inject executable markup even if its initial import was safe. Sanitize raw-HTML posts before assigning their cooked content.

URL rewriting corrupts protocol-relative links and misses relative paths

The slash-prefix rewrite treats `//cdn.example.com/image.png` as a path on the article host, producing a URL such as `https://blog.example.com/cdn.example.com/image.png`. Conversely, document-relative references such as `images/photo.png` and `../article` are left unchanged and resolve against the Discourse page rather than the imported article. Both anchor and image handling have this problem. Resolve references against the article URL using URI resolution instead of manually concatenating the host.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

false_positives.candidate:
Preserve right alignment in the legacy flexbox fallback

The new flexbox mixin explicitly falls back to `display: -webkit-box`, but that older layout model does not distribute free space to auto margins. On box-only browsers such as Android 4.3's stock browser and Safari 6, removing `float: right` and relying on `margin-left: auto` therefore leaves the navigation panel immediately after the logo/topic information instead of at the right edge. No child is given `-webkit-box-flex` to absorb the remaining space. Provide a compatible expanding spacer/item for that fallback, or retain a working non-flex layout for those browsers.

true_positives.matched_candidate:
Do not replace an omitted refresh token with a placeholder

This assignment runs even when credential sharing is disabled. Office365 explicitly permits refresh responses without `refresh_token` and merges the parsed response into the existing credentials. Adding the literal `refresh_token` therefore overwrites the user's valid refresh token when Microsoft omits a replacement, causing the next refresh to fail. Preserve the existing refresh token when no replacement is returned.

true_positives.matched_candidate:
Define actual token fields instead of stringifying Zod schemas

Using `z.string().toString()` as an object key does not define a wildcard: both computed keys evaluate to the literal `[object Object]`, and the second overwrites the first. Zod also strips unknown fields by default, so a sync response containing `access_token` and `expires_in` loses its expiry and refresh token. Zoom consequently calculates a NaN expiry, and Office365 cannot retain the new expiry. Define explicit supported expiry fields and preserve the required response properties.

Persist the parsed Google credentials, not the safeParse result

`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns `{ success: true, data: ... }`, whereas the previous `googleCredentialSchema.parse` returned the credentials themselves. Saving this result directly as `key` nests all tokens under `data`. After a successful refresh, the next GoogleCalendarService instance cannot parse the saved credentials. This also corrupts credentials when sharing is disabled; persist the result's `data` instead.

true_positives.matched_candidate:
Pass the credential owner's user ID to the sync endpoint

`refreshOAuthTokens` interprets its third argument as a user ID and sends it as `calcomUserId`, but this call passes the credential's database ID. These IDs are unrelated. The parent application will either fail to find the user or select another user's Bigin credentials. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

false_positives.candidate:
Adapt Lark refresh handling to externally managed tokens

Only the request destination changes here; the following code still expects Lark's nested `data` envelope and both `refresh_token` and `refresh_expires_in`. The helper's documented access-token-and-expiry response therefore fails parsing. Even if the parent supplies a Lark envelope with only those minimal fields, the saved credential loses its refresh token and the next refresh deletes it at the local refresh-token check. Handle synced credentials separately so the parent can own refresh tokens without Cal.com rejecting or deleting the integration.

Authenticate outbound credential requests

The request asking the parent application to return a user's OAuth access token contains only a predictable user ID and app slug. It sends neither the configured shared secret nor another authentication proof. An endpoint protected by a shared secret cannot accept these requests; an endpoint that trusts this payload alone exposes users' third-party tokens to anyone who can reach it. Add an authenticated outbound request contract rather than requiring the token-serving endpoint to trust these identifiers.

Import Prisma before using it

The new credential update references `prisma`, but this module neither imports nor declares it. This fails TypeScript checking and, if transpiled without checking, throws a ReferenceError whenever Salesforce client initialization reaches the update, preventing Salesforce operations.

Route Salesforce refreshes through the configured sync endpoint

Unlike the other adapters, Salesforce now unconditionally refreshes directly against Salesforce rather than calling `refreshOAuthTokens`. Enabling credential syncing changes its response parser but never changes the refresh destination. For credentials whose refresh token is held by the parent application, client initialization fails with an invalid refresh token even if a valid access token was synced. Use the external refresh path when configured.

Send the Zoom app slug rather than its integration directory name

The sync request sends `appSlug=zoomvideo`, but Zoom credentials are created with `appId: "zoom"`, and the inbound webhook identifies apps by their database slug. A parent application using that same app identity cannot match this refresh request to the synced Zoom credentials. Pass `zoom` here.

Support the minimal sync payload in Webex token validation

The new sync helper specifies that the endpoint should return only an access token and expiry, but this adapter still validates that response with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema`, which requires scope, token type, refresh token, and refresh-token expiry. A response following the new contract is always rejected, so synced Webex credentials stop working when their access token expires. Add a sync-specific response path that preserves existing metadata and does not require a remotely held refresh token.

true_positives.matched_candidate:
Use a portable in-place replacement for the webhook URL

The sed -i '' syntax works with BSD sed but fails with GNU sed on Linux. When GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL already exists, the replacement fails and the script still prints that it updated the file, leaving the application pointed at the previous tunnel. Use a cross-platform replacement and check its exit status before reporting success.

This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.

false_positives.candidate:
Invalidate connected calendars after deleting the cache

The delete-cache success handler only calls the optional onSuccess callback; it never invalidates the connectedCalendars query that supplies cacheUpdatedAt. The wrapper does not provide a default refetch callback and disables refetchOnWindowFocus, so a successful deletion can leave the old timestamp and Delete cached data action visible until the page is reloaded. Invalidate connectedCalendars after deletion, as the disconnect mutation already does.

Resolve persistent cache records for in-memory delegated credentials

For delegated connections represented by negative, in-memory credential IDs, querying CalendarCache by the displayed credentialId cannot find their cache records. The cache repository explicitly supports serving these connections from persistent records using userId and the calendar key instead. Consequently, a delegated calendar can actively serve cached availability while this endpoint returns cacheUpdatedAt: null, hiding both status and deletion controls. Resolve the corresponding persistent cache records within the current user's scope and support that same mapping in the deletion handler.

Resolve the environment file relative to the script

ENV_FILE="../.env" is relative to the caller's working directory, not the script's directory. Running bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repository root therefore creates or modifies .env in the repository's parent directory rather than the application's environment file. The script reports success, but the application never receives GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL. Derive the repository path from BASH_SOURCE before selecting the environment file.

Keep the registered metric alert handler instantiable

Build the expected occurrence for the group key being evaluated

TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds its expected occurrence using group key "val1", but calls evaluate_group_key_value with "group_key". The occurrence builder includes that key in the fingerprint, so the expected occurrence has fingerprint '<detector id>:val1' while the actual occurrence has '<detector id>:group_key'. true_positives.matched_candidate:
Spawned workers fail the process type check and are never killed

Workers are created with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, whose SpawnProcess class is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process. This isinstance check therefore returns false for production workers, skipping kill() before starting a replacement. A hung worker remains alive and can resume flushing the same shards concurrently with its replacement, causing duplicate production and leaking processes across restarts. The same check in join() also skips termination. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or the actual spawn-context process class instead.

true_positives.golden_comment: Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Terminate remaining workers after the join deadline expires

When next_step.join() or an earlier worker consumes the shutdown timeout, this break skips every remaining worker, including their termination logic. Setting the shared stopped flag does not interrupt a worker blocked in Redis or future.result(), so those workers can survive a rebalance and later flush shards now owned by another consumer. Once the deadline expires, stop waiting but still terminate and reap all remaining workers.

With one slot remaining, concurrent requests from distinct new devices can both observe a count below the limit and both insert successfully. Those devices then remain eligible for updates even though the configured cap has been exceeded. Serialize the count-and-admit operation across requests and Grafana instances using appropriate database locking or an equivalent atomic admission mechanism.
